name: Jensen Huang
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The birthplace of the compute inflection, but the pre-training window has been locked up by big companies' compute, and a student can hardly get in from scratch
D01.late_modes: Training a general foundation model from scratch to start a company or publish papers; the compute barrier has been locked up by big companies
D01.conflict: NVIDIA sells compute; the more compute pre-training burns, the better for him

D02.one_line: Reasoning is what he called the second exponential; the RL/reasoning lever is the largest, and small compute can still produce landmark work (s1)
D02.late_modes: Directly replicating the standard RLHF pipeline; it is already a commoditized baseline
D02.conflict: Reasoning demand is what he called the second exponential, and it directly drives compute sales

D03.one_line: Agents have large prospects, but self-modification needs a human in the loop; the pure continual-learning/memory part remains open
D03.conflict: Agents drive inference compute, which favors his demand narrative

D04.one_line: Scaffolding will be absorbed by platform runtimes, which the SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench data already confirm
D04.late_modes: Building a pure wrapper-layer agent demo to raise money; it will be absorbed by platform runtimes
D04.conflict: Runtimes such as OpenClaw are pushed by NVIDIA's own ecosystem, and he has praised them by name

D05.one_line: Necessary trust infrastructure, not an engine of progress; academic independence is an advantage, but it is being commercialized (Arena)
D05.late_modes: Only chasing public leaderboard rank; it is being eroded by leaderboard gaming and contamination from proprietary data

D06.one_line: Physical AI is what he called the next ten-trillion-dollar market
D06.late_modes: Chasing eye-catching humanoid demos without reliability/intervention-rate metrics; easily copied by faster teams
D06.conflict: GR00T, robot computers and Physical AI are the new market he is betting on

D07.one_line: WAM-style action generation is the GR00T route, and academic recipes (diffusion policy and others) have been shown to be adoptable
D07.late_modes: Only replicating the published diffusion policy recipe as a baseline; it is no longer an incremental contribution
D07.conflict: Products such as GR00T map directly onto this direction

D08.one_line: The world model is the core of his grounding logic, and it is getting hotter and more expensive (AMI Labs $3.5 billion)
D08.late_modes: Only chasing the realism of video frames; the generation side is being commoditized
D08.conflict: Cosmos is his open-model product, and the world-model narrative supports his compute sales

D09.one_line: Simulation is his deepest path dependence (RIVA128), and the real bottleneck for closing the physical-data gap
D09.conflict: Omniverse/Isaac Sim/DSX Air are his simulation product line

D10.one_line: Robotaxi is starting to scale, but it is increasingly a game of a few platforms and their fleet data
D10.late_modes: Making incremental improvements in the style of L2 driver-assistance features; carmakers have already made them standard
D10.conflict: The DRIVE platform and the partnership with Uber are among his revenue lines

D11.one_line: The gaps exposed by understanding benchmarks are real (BLINK/VSI-Bench), but it is not the layer he talks about most

D12.one_line: Generation is being commoditized, and consumer-side sustainability is in doubt (Sora2 went offline less than a year after launch)
D12.late_modes: Building a pure consumer-grade text-to-image/text-to-video app; Sora2's shutdown is a ready-made counterexample

D13.one_line: He treats safety as an engineering-redundancy problem and distrusts closed-door work; the technical details of mechanistic interpretability are not his strong suit
D13.late_modes: Only patching known jailbreaks after the fact; defense lags attack structurally
D13.conflict: Publicly disagrees with Amodei; he argues for openness and against a few people doing safety behind closed doors

D14.one_line: Extreme co-design is his bedrock, and FlashAttention-style contributions have extremely high leverage

D15.one_line: GPUs are what he called a time machine for science

D16.one_line: Generative recommendation consumes compute, which favors him, but he has never directly discussed this vertical, so confidence is low

lever_reason: Simulation plus world models fill the physical-data gap, RL turns reasoning into the second exponential, and systems efficiency keeps scaling going; evaluation is necessary but not the engine.

Q2.condition: Choose a narrow-domain model (VLA/world model, not general LLM pre-training), with independent third-party evaluation, a team of 2-4, and open weights that outsiders can adopt

cruxes.question: Should evaluation rank first, or is it only infrastructure?
cruxes.my_position: Necessary but not the engine; what really decides progress is simulation, world models and test-time compute
cruxes.would_change_if: An evaluation or judge method is shown to predict new failure modes that have not been systematically tested, not just re-check known benchmarks

cruxes.question: Can simulation fill the robot data gap, especially for contact and touch?
cruxes.my_position: For non-contact tasks it mostly can; for contact-rich, touch-dependent tasks, I may be overestimating how much simulation covers
cruxes.would_change_if: A purely data-driven world model, not conditioned on simulation, catches up with simulation-conditioned models on contact counterfactuals

cruxes.question: Without large compute, can academia still make adopted contributions on foundation models?
cruxes.my_position: On general pre-training, almost not; with a narrow-domain model, open weights, independent evaluation and a small team, yes
cruxes.would_change_if: A narrow-domain model (VLA/world model) from an academic lab or small team is widely adopted by industry on independent evaluation

taste_advice: Pick interfaces that can be reused across generations; do not bet on a single product; CUDA taking about ten years to pay back proves the point

pairwise.why: The world model is the core of grounding; evaluation is necessary but not the engine
Physical AI is a ten-trillion-dollar-scale market; evaluation is only infrastructure
Embodied AI is the destination and the world model is the method; the destination carries more weight
WAM builds perception into a world model and then attaches actions, which is more fundamental than a plain policy head
Physical AI is the destination; simulation is only a method for filling the data gap
RL/reasoning is the second exponential; self-improvement is still bound by the human-in-the-loop red line
Generation benchmarks are being commoditized; understanding gaps are more real and more lasting
The pre-training window has been locked up by big companies; evaluation still has room for independence
A pure wrapper layer will be absorbed by platforms; continual learning itself remains open
Safety is an engineering-redundancy problem; the value of evaluation independence is more direct
Autonomous driving is narrowing to a few platforms; physical AI is the bigger bet
